recipes.name: Caramel Macchiato Cheesecake
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup brewed espresso or strong coffee

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly coat a 9-inch springform pan with nonstick cooking spray.

Mix together the graham cracker crumbs, melted butter, and 2 tablespoons of sugar until well combined. Press into the bottom of the prepared springform pan, and 1 inch up the sides. Bake in preheated oven for 8 minutes, then remove to cool on a wire rack.
Reduce oven temperature to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

Beat the softened cream cheese in a large bowl with an electric mixer until fluffy. Gradually add 1 cup of sugar, beating until blended. Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Stir in sour cream, espresso and vanilla. Pour batter into the baked and cooled crust.

Bake cheesecake in the preheated oven for 1 hour and 5 minutes; then turn the oven off, partially open the door and allow the cheesecake to rest for 15 minutes more. Remove from the oven, and run a knife around the edges. Cool cheesecake on a wire rack to room temperature, then cover the springform pan with plastic wrap, and chill in the refrigerator for 8 hours.
To serve, cut the cheesecake into wedges and garnish each slice with whipped cream and caramel sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Caramel Macchiato Cheesecake
raw_recipe.description: I work at a coffee shop and my favorite coffee drink is a caramel macchiato so I created a caramel macchiato cheesecake that has become my favorite cheesecake.

review.reviewBody: I'm Dawn's husband, Kevin. For over 20 years, I've been the winner. Dawn puts so much into her cooking and loves putting new dishes in front of us all the time. The Carmel Macchiato Cheesecake is another in a long line of great recipes Dawn has come up with. It's the best desert I've had and, thanks to Dawn, I've had a lot of great deserts!

This. Was. Amazing. After reading some reviews, I opted for crushing chocolate teddy grahams for the crust and added 1 tsp instant espresso granules to the crust. I also doubled the espresso in the filling, and added 2 Tbsp caramel. I took the suggestion of placing the springform pan on a muffin tin pan filled with water, and I left it in the oven a few hours after turning it off. It turned out perfectly! So smooth and cream, no cracks, and a wonderful blend of flavors! 

I topped with homemade caramel - melt 1 stick butter and 1 C brown sugar, boiling about 5 minutes until smooth. Turn off heat and add 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp vanilla and enough evaporated milk until it reaches desired consistency - about 1/2 cup (will thicken as it cools).

Other than baking this in a water bath and switching the oven off and leaving the cheesecake in there for a couple of hours, I made this recipe exactly as directed. I decorated the top with a stabilized whipped cream and Ghirardelli caramel sauce. It was delicious and tasted SO SO much like a caramel macchiato. I brought this to a neighbors house for dinner, and everyone loved it. The coffee flavor was definitely there (I used Lavazza crema e' gusto brewed espresso). It was level, with no cracks. No need to mess with this recipe. It's perfect as is.

All I can say is, LOVE IT!! I've been making cheesecake for years, and I was soooo happy to see the suggestion of sitting the spring form pan on top of a muffin tin filled with water as your "water bath". How easy is that?! And it works! Also followed other reviewer's thoughts on the cinnamon in the crust, using strong espresso from a coffee shop, and leaving it in the turned off oven with door slightly propped open for another hour. Creamy cake, no cracking. I also, due to dietary issues, made mine like I always do with Tofutti brand Better than Cream Cheese for the cheese and their Sour Supreme (both non-dairy products) and everyone loves it. You would never know it's not dairy. Thank you Dawn for this wonderful recipe. Coffee and caramel, what's not to love?!

A complete hit at our holiday/birthday dinner with family. I followed the recipe and also baked in a water bath, and cooled down in the oven for a couple of hours. Turned out perfectly. I changed up the topping by making a fruit glaze of blueberry, lime, and peach preserves pureed together with a TSP of corn starch added to thicken, and then topped off with fresh blackberries. Lastly, made fresh whipped vanilla cream for topping (not that it really needed it). The background flavor of the coffee really sets it apart from other cheesecake recipes I've tried. It has officially become a new birthday/holiday tradition!

I made this for a coworker's birthday and it received rave reviews. I followed the recipe for ingredients to a tee. I did bake it in a waterbath for about 65 minutes and then let it cool for an hour and covered with foil and refrigerated. The crust came out perfect, firm but tender to cut. NO CRACKS!! The espresso flavor is not too strong and tamed by the sweetness of the caramel sauce. 

I used Hershey's caramel syrup and homemade whipped cream (heavy cream, 2 tbsp. powdered sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla).

I've discovered a tip for doing a water bath while using a spring form pan and since I've yet to see a review or recipe with this tip in it I'm going to tell all my food loving friends. Put your spring form in a slow cooker liner bag then put it in your water bath. Leave the bag open and roll the edges down towards the rim of your cheese cake pan. Works like a CHARM and works like a hammock when lifting the cake out of the water when done.
This is super easy to make. I add a bit of instant espresso to my graham cracker crust and I make a coffee whipped cream for the top

So yummy, made 18 mini cheese cakes instead of one. Pressed crust into muffin tins with liners then took liners off before serving. Baked for about 20 min Topped with Carmel and whipped cream.. So good. Just a touch of coffee flavour nice fluffy creamy texture.

I have made this many times. Thank you Dawn for an amazing recipe. 
First few times--- followed recipe exactly --- many cracks.
Next few times --- tried putting pan of water on bottom rack so oven has moisture, still cracked.
Then tried making a water bath with my too small aluminum foil (all leaked inside and soggy crust)
Finally tonight I actually got some oversized aluminum foil from Costco and cheesecake turned out absolutely fantastic with no cracks.
Overall excellent, excellent delicious recipe, but make sure to do the water bath.

This is a good recipe as is but instead of just drizzling caramel on top I set aside 1 cup of the cream cheese mixture with everything mixed but the coffee and add caramel to the 1 cup. I than add the coffee to the remaining batter then put the espresso later on the bottom and top with the caramel cheesecake.

I hesitated making this cheesecake for I have been making the same one for years and they always turned out great. I do have some tips for success that is all ingredients must be room tempature. When you mix the cream cheese at room temp it is smooth if it is cold you will get little clumps that are not smooth. Once creamy add eggs one at a time . try to do that gently you don't want air in batter.
Made as a special request for a birthday
I followed the recipe exactly and it came out perfectly. I too added real whipped cream with expresso granules to decorate the edge along with pecans.

I’ve made this cheesecake for the past several Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays and we have enjoyed it thoroughly! I always make sure to use a water bath when baking. The instructions are easy to follow and the taste is wonderful.

I made this cheesecake for a Super Bowl family party. It was a real hit. People took seconds! I substituted Splenda for the sugar and used sugar-free caramel sauce. Nobody knew any different. There was sugar in the graham crackers that I used to make the crust. I used my smallest Italian stove-top coffee pot to make the 1/4 cup brew. I'll be making this cheesecake again!
Super easy. Great rich flavor. My favorite cheesecake. I made it for a dessert auction and have had several more requests for it!
Fabulous!!! I watch the video to remember exactly how Dawn makes this recipe, and then I make the cheesecake for my husband’s Birthday each year. It is his favorite dessert! He loves it!

I have made this multiple times. The recipe is spot on. I have good friends who treat themselves to caramel macchiato at SB weekly and make this for their birthdays annually. Even no coffee lovers gobble this up! As with all my cheeses cakes, I wrap the bottom of the springform with foil, just in case there’s a butter leak, and place on a cookie sheet with water bath to prevent dryness and cracking. I don’t give 5 stars easily…this deserves it!
